title: Hello, Python!
explanation: The print() function shows text in the Output panel. Text inside quotes is called a string.
challenge: Change the message so Python prints something about you.
hint: Keep your message between the quotation marks.

title: Remember values
explanation: A variable gives a value a memorable name. Python uses = to store the value on its right.
challenge: Create a second variable for your favorite color and print it.
hint: Follow the favorite_food example, using a new variable name.

title: Ask a question
explanation: input() pauses the program for an answer. PyNivo lets you type that answer below the Output panel.
code:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print(f"Nice to meet you, {name}!")
challenge: Ask the learner for their favorite hobby and respond to it.
hint: Store the result of a second input() call in a variable.

title: Make a decision
explanation: An if statement runs indented code only when its condition is true. else handles the other case.
challenge: Add a special message when age is exactly 13.
hint: Put an elif age == 13 branch between if and else.

title: Repeat with loops
explanation: for loops repeat code for each value; while loops continue while a condition remains true.
challenge: Print only the even numbers from 2 through 10.

title: Organize with lists
explanation: Lists keep ordered collections that can grow, shrink, and be changed.
code:
tasks = ["learn lists", "write code"]
tasks.append("run program")
for task in tasks:
    print(task)
challenge: Remove one task and print how many remain.

title: Fixed collections
explanation: Tuples are ordered collections whose items cannot be replaced after creation.
code:
point = (4, 7)
x, y = point
print(f"x={x}, y={y}")
challenge: Create an RGB color tuple and unpack it.
hint: A tuple uses commas: red, green, blue = (255, 80, 20).

title: Label data with dictionaries
explanation: Dictionaries connect unique keys to values, making related data easy to find.
challenge: Add a language key and display it.

title: Keep unique values
explanation: Sets store unique items and make membership and overlap checks concise.
challenge: Find the shared values in two sets.

title: Build reusable functions
explanation: Functions name a reusable block of work. Parameters receive values and return sends a result back.
challenge: Write a function that converts minutes to seconds.

title: Use modules
explanation: Modules organize reusable code. Python's standard library is available offline.
code:
import random

secret = random.randint(1, 10)
print(f"Secret number: {secret}")

title: Read and write files
explanation: with safely closes a file after reading or writing. Encoding keeps text predictable.
code:
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("message.txt")
path.write_text("Hello from Python!", encoding="utf-8")
print(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
challenge: Write three lines to a file and read them back.

title: Handle errors
explanation: try and except let a program respond to expected problems without crashing.
challenge: Add a finally block that always says Goodbye.
hint: finally belongs after the except blocks.

title: Transform collections
explanation: A comprehension builds a collection from another iterable in one readable expression.
code:
squares = [number ** 2 for number in range(1, 6)]
print(squares)
challenge: Create a list containing only even squares.

title: Create your own objects
explanation: A class describes data and behavior that belong together. Each instance is a separate object.
challenge: Add an age attribute and a birthday method.

title: Extend classes
explanation: Inheritance lets a specialized class reuse and adapt behavior from a parent class.
challenge: Create a Dog subclass with its own sound.

title: Check your code
explanation: Assertions document expectations and reveal mistakes early. Larger projects use test frameworks such as pytest.
code:
def add(left, right):
    return left + right

assert add(2, 3) == 5
print("All checks passed!")
challenge: Add checks for negative numbers and zero.

title: Build a quiz game
explanation: This project combines input, collections, loops, conditions, and score tracking.
challenge: Add two questions and show encouraging feedback.
